:REASON:       All five HIGH blocking findings and both MEDIUM closed, across two workers. The continuation inherited d982af1 (the WIP the manager preserved when the writer outage killed the first worker) and found it substantially complete but UNGATED — it built clean and its focused suites were already green, and cargo fmt having never run is the marker of exactly where that worker was interrupted. Its own work was the gap between written and provable: fmt, three clippy errors, the finding-6 regression the WIP was killed before writing (surfaced by clippy as an uncalled cfg(test) accessor, then verified red on BOTH halves of the guard independently), and three of four injection artifacts re-cut because this round rewrote the code they inject onto. The author re-ran the binary extraction independently (byte offset 238701938) rather than trusting the reviewer or the manager, and recorded a trap worth keeping: the frames ship as JS escapes, never UTF-8, so grepping the glyph itself returns nothing — a plausible way for a future re-derivation to conclude wrongly. It swept all six other U+2736 sites to confirm the frame arrays are the only spinner. The old positive control was a tautology (it walked the table and asserted the table's own entries), which is precisely how the missing frame survived a review round; the new controls name the frames independently of the table, and a completeness guard streams the installed binary, decodes both sequences and asserts superset. All four of the guard's paths were exercised on this host, including a 1 MiB size floor so the rmux PATH shim cannot trip the needle-absent failure. A real rmux pane now paints the frame and it is proven load-bearing. Gates run with the TASK-NTNK0 PATH correction and the sentinel quoted. No unmet criteria; four residual risks declared.

:REASON:       Three P1 process tasks landed as one coherent text rather than three appends to the same 119 lines. YGB1R gives four countable triggers and a floor rule, deletes the 'if the tier is unclear, ask the user' escape hatch that was the mechanism it existed to remove, and states plainly that the tier is computed so there is no decision to bring the user. 4YX1K defines the confirm class by property with the proceed class named explicitly, and carries the scope-and-expiry nuance verbatim. TW3N3 states the committed-history precondition as one constraint with two halves and adds the branch-collision trap this session hit twice. The calibration table is the check that matters: the rule classifies its own dispatch as ordinary, which is exactly how it was run. Three criteria are unmet and declared — YGB1R item 4 needs TASK-3CM0Q's verb to emit a computed tier, TW3N3 item 3's dispatch guard is Rust and out of scope (filed separately), and TW3N3 item 4 had no grill/review file to extend. The author also corrected the brief: my calibration example described TASK-15MJN as a duplicate cancellation, which is what I DID to it, not what its heading says; it calibrated against the live heading and that mismatch surfaced a real defect in its trigger-2 wording.

* TX 2026-08-02 Sun 23:50:55 implementer.done TASK-FZB6T.3
:PROPERTIES:
:TX_ID:        tx-20260802-orgasmic-4230

:PROJECT:      orgasmic
:TASK:         TASK-FZB6T.3
:REASON:       All five round-2 findings closed with real machinery rather than narrowed residuals. The fence became a lease held ACROSS the rename — a Session command for a leased path is deferred before anything is opened and runs after the rename and journal write — with a regression that spins on the writer's deferred count rather than sleeping, so it is provably a pre-rename append, and asserts both halves. The manifest is versioned with both shapes decoding, and a plan naming files with no per-file record in ANY readable shape is now refused, which is exactly the shape each runtime saw of the other's and called a successful rollback. The scanner validates per RFC 8259 and is cross-checked against serde_json in BOTH directions, so hardening did not quietly stop reclaiming real payload. dec_BBPW4 took a side: tombstones persist outside the disposable cache, merged never replaced. The split injection was confirmed from the red log rather than inferred. It also fixed six daemon tests that were RED ON MAIN before it started — broken by TASK-FZB6T.2, which I merged and closed — proven by checking 1393e06 into a scratch worktree and reproducing identical panics. My own gate missed that because I ran focused filters to spare the machine; that tradeoff has now been paid once and is recorded.

:PROPERTIES:
:TX_ID:        tx-20260803-orgasmic-4275
:TIME:         [2026-08-03 Mon 00:47:48]
:TYPE:         reviewer.done
:ACTOR:        agent.reviewer
:MACHINE:      Vasyls-MacBook-Pro.local
:PROJECT:      orgasmic
:TASK:         TASK-FZB6T
:REASON:       Round 3. The sharpest finding reopens what round 3 closed: post_run_history_compact holds the SessionLease in the HTTP handler while awaiting spawn_blocking, and a started blocking task is NOT cancelled when its join handle is dropped — so a client disconnect drops the lease while the transaction is still between its final fingerprint check and rename, making the orphaned-inode race live again. The regression cannot catch it because it holds the lease manually. It also found that Rust's is_ascii_whitespace includes 0x0b and 0x0c while JSON permits only four bytes, so a record serde_json rejects is classified reclaimable and deleted — and the 19-case two-way cross-check omits exactly those bytes. This reviewer also served as the TASK-48SFW discriminator and completed untouched, which exonerates the dispatch path.
:MODEL:        gpt-5.6-sol
:EFFORT:       high
:WALL:         20m
:REVIEWED_DIFF: 0bdfaed..84e4257
:MODEL:        gpt-5.6-sol
:EFFORT:       high
:VERDICT:      NEEDS FIXES — BLOCK SHIP
:FINDINGS:     4 P1 blocking (request cancellation drops the lease while spawn_blocking continues; tombstone ledger not fail-closed and neither locked nor fsynced; JSON validator accepts vertical tab and form feed which serde_json rejects; rollback not bound to one validated manifest/archive generation), 1 P2 (machine-specific absolute paths in a repo-root file)

:REASON:       Third dispatch-wide outage. Root cause now confirmed IN SOURCE rather than inferred: ensure_running -> start_via_selected_adapter -> daemon_service::start, whose macOS adapter writes and loads ~/Library/LaunchAgents/orgasmic.daemon.plist — a per-user path ORGASMIC_HOME does not scope. Any orgasmic verb that needs a daemon, run against a staged home whose daemon is not up, therefore restarts the REAL daemon and kills every live run. TASK-VEGRV was live in all three outages and died 4-6 minutes in each time, exactly at its render check; the manager's own brief instructed that render check, including the supposedly safe rewrite.

:REASON:       Fourth blocking round. The three P1s are each a real resurrect-or-lose-evidence path: boot reattach never consults worktree_authority so a durably tombstoned run can be auto-reattached after a restart even though /api/runs refuses it; refresh_dir applies ledger authority only to freshly rebuilt entries so a cache hit lets stale Verified state beat the durable no-attach fact; and rollback computes its lease from one unlocked manifest read then decodes a different generation under the lock, with no fence assertion, recreating the orphaned-inode window the lease exists to prevent. The P2 is safe-failing — rollback refuses rather than overwriting — but means legacy rollback is unavailable in a classifier-drift case. THE PATTERN IS NOW THE FINDING: every one of these lives in machinery a previous round introduced to satisfy a previous finding.

:PROJECT:      orgasmic
:TASK:         TASK-3CM0Q
:REASON:       The verb exists and the default is inverted. Its best decision is the asymmetry on re-declaration: growth re-declares upward with no flag and no permission, because the tier is computed from countable triggers and a recomputation is not a decision anyone can approve — but LOWERING is refused without --lower and a reason stating the first declaration was wrong, since 'it looked smaller once I was inside it' is the exact rationalization the floor rule exists to stop and must not be spellable as a fresh computation. On the inherited WIP it found the daemon half complete but entirely unwired with no test, and the CLI verb non-existent; it verified the handler against the acceptance rather than trusting it. It also found the SAFE way to drive a real daemon from a test — ORGASMIC_DAEMON_URL on the child makes ensure_running return before any adapter start — which is the pattern TASK-48SFW's three outages should have used, and the manager confirmed the plist mtime was unchanged after running it.

:TASK:         TASK-8ED6V
:REASON:       One table in core owns the retired-content families and every surface reads it, so a future cutover is one edit rather than four to remember. The maintenance discipline is ENFORCED rather than documented: a test fails when a table entry is not named in the shipped router with its deciding node, so a cutover author cannot land the code without the agent-facing text in the same release. The author declined the more elegant :RETIRES_PATHS: decision-property trigger with a real reason — a dispatch worktree's .orgasmic/ is a frozen snapshot, so that test would pass vacuously on the branch and fail after merge. Removal is a separate flag rather than part of --fix because --fix repairs runtime-owned things while this deletes operator-written content, and for the same reason it is not on the upgrade path. Manager verified the doctor output behaviourally against staged residue rather than trusting the tests.

Answer to the question asked: the gate is MERELY LESS VACUOUS, not protective -- 6 values over 3 of 9 real enum sites; the reviewer poisoned the other 6 SIMULTANEOUSLY and the suite stayed green. * TX 2026-08-06 Thu 12:23:18 reviewer.done TASK-ZBYH3
:PROPERTIES:
:TX_ID:        tx-20260806-orgasmic-4836
:TIME:         [2026-08-06 Thu 12:23:18]
:TYPE:         reviewer.done
:ACTOR:        agent.reviewer
:MACHINE:      Vasyls-MacBook-Pro.local
:PROJECT:      orgasmic
:TASK:         TASK-ZBYH3
:REASON:       REJECT, 1 BLOCK SHIP. Rulings A and B CONFLICT rather than compose, and the manager's own task body asserted they compose -- that framing is the defect's origin. B suppresses the mirror only when fd 1 and the durable path share device+inode; A moves StandardOutPath to a DIFFERENT inode. So after the next daemon start / reinstall rewrites the plist, stdout_same_as_path returns false, LogMirror::Stdout survives, and the full tracing stream is written to BOTH daemon.out.log (rotated) and daemon.stdout.log (rotated by nothing, pruned by nothing, read by nothing, named in no error message) -- roughly 300MB/year. Total write volume and disk growth are UNCHANGED from the pre-fix defect; only the distribution moved. Worse on Windows, where same_file_as_path is cfg(not(unix)) -> false so B can never fire. Both mandated answers came back clean and probe-verified: interactive serve still prints to a tty, and NO programmatic reader of daemon.out.log exists, so no boot diagnostic goes quiet. Recommended fix is to gate the mirror on is_terminal ONLY when a durable sink exists -- which subsumes B and survives A. F3 is the other one that matters: a failed reopen after a SUCCESSFUL roll silences the durable log permanently with no retry AND stops record_drop moving, so the degradation is invisible through the very counter designated for it.
:MODEL:        claude-opus-5
:EFFORT:       high
:REVIEWED_DIFF: 9eea11f..145fb89
:VERDICT:      reject

:PROPERTIES:

:PROJECT:      orgasmic
:TASK:         TASK-ZBYH3.1
:REASON:       APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS, no BLOCK SHIP. The relocated double-write is fixed and proven on the PRODUCTION discriminator for the first time in this chain. Both mandated answers came back confirming the manager's suspicions with numbers. (1) is_terminal is still a PROXY -- it answers 'is fd 1 a tty', not 'will this land somewhere nothing rotates'. Much better than inode equality (correct for all three shipped service definitions plus the detached fallback, and works on Windows where the inode check was hardcoded false), but it fails both ways: a pty-backed capture (script/unbuffer/docker -t) RESTORES the defect class, and 'orgasmic serve | tee' now silently drops stdout tracing -- a live behaviour change from main, though both in-repo consumers are safe because the startup banner bypasses the tracing sink. (2) The F3 retry is UNBOUNDED and worse than a bare per-line open: in the stuck state each log line costs ~2 open + ~2 create_dir_all + up to 31 stats + 1 rename + 3 stderr writes, all under the sink mutex, with 4x record_drop inflation -- reproduced 1:1 from the project's own test stderr. That is the same unbounded-unrotated-growth shape this chain exists to remove, at ~3x the rate, into daemon.err.log which nothing rotates. Filed as the next round.

* TX 2026-08-06 Thu 13:53:18 reviewer.done TASK-G64ZH
:PROPERTIES:
:TX_ID:        tx-20260806-orgasmic-4877
:TIME:         [2026-08-06 Thu 13:53:18]
:TYPE:         reviewer.done
:ACTOR:        agent.reviewer
:MACHINE:      Vasyls-MacBook-Pro.local
:PROJECT:      orgasmic
:TASK:         TASK-G64ZH
:REASON:       REJECT, two BLOCK SHIP, both verified against the code by the manager. F-A: with --no-log-mirror in the service definitions, a boot-time durable-open failure is TOTAL SILENCE — init_tracing_to's and_then discards the path with the handle, resolve_mirror's durable-absent early return hands back the caller's LogMirror::None, and durable_path=None makes the new backoff unreachable forever; pre-diff the caller passed Stdout unconditionally so every line landed in launchd's StandardOutPath. The most likely production trigger gets none of the fix. F-B: the generated plist/unit/wrapper embed --no-log-mirror, so a manual runtime rollback (update.rs keeps one previous install for exactly that) gives an old binary an unknown flag under KeepAlive=true — a launchd crash loop writing clap usage into the unrotated daemon.err.log, the same growth shape this chain exists to remove, on a daemon that is DOWN. The env form is already implemented and an old binary ignores it. Non-blocking: F-C the rename branch stays per-line (pre-existing, not a regression, mint a follow-up), F-D the F3 seam moved rather than closed, F-E only the backoff ceiling is pinned not the floor, F-F the env parser has no test at all.
:MODEL:        claude-opus-5
:EFFORT:       high
:VERDICT:      reject
:CLOSED_TX:    tx-20260806-orgasmic-4873
:LIFECYCLE_FROM: in_review
:LIFECYCLE_TO: in_progress
:CLEANUP_STATUS: ok
:END:

* TX 2026-08-06 Thu 14:22:29 reviewer.done TASK-G64ZH.1
:PROPERTIES:
:TX_ID:        tx-20260806-orgasmic-4897
:TIME:         [2026-08-06 Thu 14:22:29]
:TYPE:         reviewer.done
:ACTOR:        agent.reviewer
:MACHINE:      Vasyls-MacBook-Pro.local
:PROJECT:      orgasmic
:TASK:         TASK-G64ZH.1
:REASON:       REJECT, two BLOCK SHIP, both verified by the manager. R-1 (NEW, this round): the type change to Option<(PathBuf, Option<File>)> dropped the invariant 'durable_path is Some implies a live handle', which resolve_mirror still depends on — so a failed boot open now trips the is_terminal() gate and silences EVERY non-terminal launch, not just a mirror-suppressed one (hand-rolled systemd, docker entrypoint, supervisord, nohup, plain 'serve >> capture.log'). Strictly wider than F-A, and no test covers it: the one that looks like the guard passes durable=None, which is ABSENT not FAILED. R-2: F-A's total-silence half is not dead — a permanently unopenable path under suppression still writes zero bytes anywhere. Both share one fix: gate the mirror on the HANDLE, not the PATH. F-B IS dead, verified against the actual rollback target: an old binary boots normally on the new plist and reaches byte-identical behaviour. Non-blocking: R-3 the F-E test is self-referential (it reads next_reopen_attempt out of state then sets the clock to it, so a deadline of now+86400s passes all 15 tests), R-4 the reopen retry writes a stderr line per attempt into the unrotated daemon.err.log (~47MB/year at the 60s cap) and should be throttled rather than removed since it is the operator's only diagnostic in the R-2 case.
:MODEL:        claude-opus-5
:EFFORT:       high
:VERDICT:      reject
:CLOSED_TX:    tx-20260806-orgasmic-4892

:LIFECYCLE_TO: in_progress

* TX 2026-08-06 Thu 14:53:54 reviewer.done TASK-G64ZH.1.1
:PROPERTIES:
:TX_ID:        tx-20260806-orgasmic-4917
:TIME:         [2026-08-06 Thu 14:53:54]
:TYPE:         reviewer.done
:ACTOR:        agent.reviewer
:MACHINE:      Vasyls-MacBook-Pro.local
:PROJECT:      orgasmic
:TASK:         TASK-G64ZH.1.1
:REASON:       APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS. Every acceptance bullet met, nothing blocking, and the first round in this chain that introduced NO new silence and NO new double-write. The dynamic fix ended the class: total silence is dead in every state reachable through a durable-open failure — boot, post-roll, transient, permanent, suppressed and unsuppressed. Rotation leaks ZERO lines, by ordering not luck: the mirror decision at :588-608 reads durable.is_none() before maybe_rotate drops the handle at :713, all inside one mutex hold, so no line observes the mid-rotation None. Steady-state double-write is dead by construction — stdout writes only when durable.is_none(), and when it is None nothing was written durably, so the two are mutually exclusive. The proof retarget is sound and was ruled independently: expect-red byte-identical, and .ok() maps Err->None so the injection is semantically identical. All three injections still apply to HEAD, verified with git apply --check. Fallback cost measured rather than estimated: 56KB/day on this host, ~10MiB/day upper bound at the rotation ceiling, against zero bytes anywhere as the alternative. Follow-ups, all non-blocking: F-1 handle PRESENCE is still a proxy for write SUCCESS (a live handle whose write_all fails loses the line and permanently short-circuits reopen) — pre-existing; F-2 the R-4 throttle test passes with the throttle deleted; F-3 alternating error kinds defeat the throttle; F-4 spawn_detached points process stdout at the durable path; F-5 dropped_log_writes now counts preserved lines.
:MODEL:        claude-opus-5
:EFFORT:       high
:VERDICT:      approve-with-follow-ups

* TX 2026-08-06 Thu 15:44:32 reviewer.done TASK-QGWK7
:PROPERTIES:
:TX_ID:        tx-20260806-orgasmic-4952
:TIME:         [2026-08-06 Thu 15:44:32]
:TYPE:         reviewer.done

:MACHINE:      Vasyls-MacBook-Pro.local
:PROJECT:      orgasmic
:TASK:         TASK-QGWK7
:REASON:       APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS, nine findings, none blocking. NO CLOSE PATH DESTROYS A REPORT ANY MORE — the two remaining deleting call sites are failed-dispatch rollback where no worker ran; verified end-to-end on the production path. F-1 HIGH: acceptance criterion 2 (readable from a fresh clone) is UNMET — the destination is trackable but nothing stages it, so durability is a sentence in a convention. Ruling: close should git add the dir (staging, not committing, leaving WHEN to commit with the manager). MANAGER CORRECTION TO ITS EVIDENCE: the review inferred from five sampled commits that no manager habit would sweep it in, but those commits cannot discriminate — dispatch-records did not exist yet, so nothing untracked was there to sweep. Tested directly: 'git add -A .orgasmic', this session's actual command, DOES stage it; 'git add -u' does not. The finding stands and the ruling stands, because the guarantee currently rests on an unstated detail of which add form a manager happens to use, which is worse than a documented step. F-2 MEDIUM with decisive arithmetic: 14.2 dispatch generations/day measured (5200-6500/yr); last.txt is 24-30MB/yr and fine, but stdout.log at the observed 157.7KB stdio mean is 820MB-1.03GB/yr uncompressed against a repo whose entire packed history is 8.71MiB — 10-25x the repo, unrotatable because pruning git history rewrites every clone. Ruling: promote a bounded tail (64KB) with the original byte count recorded, or promote only on non-success, and skip 0-byte files. F-3/F-4 MEDIUM: the --no-worktree-remove promote takes neither the cleanup lock nor the close guard yet is now destructive (it unlinks), and it flips CLEANUP_STATUS ok->partial on an already-reclaimed worktree. F-5 orphan reclaim never promotes — the rescued-dispatch case. F-6 the finalize REPORT_PATH fallback writes an absolute user-specific path into a committed tx. F-7 the copy buffers the whole artifact in RSS. F-8 a half-succeeded promote leaves last.txt promoted but no REPORT_PATH on the tx, plus .promoting leftovers. F-9 the new branch has no test, so F-3 and F-4 are invisible to the suite.

:kind:         correctness
:blocks_ship:  yes

:evidence:     implementer F9: daemon --lib subset, 51.4s wall, syspolicyd delta +49.33s on a calm host (BEFORE 4.13) = 49% of the threshold in under a minute; reviewer-measured ambient rate on this Mac 0.0753 s/s over 60s idle
:failure:      cargo build is INSIDE the sampled window (HOST_BEFORE :591 -> cargo test :595 -> HOST_AFTER :598); default CARGO_ARGS is --workspace; CI Suite runs the whole workspace with a cold build under timeout-minutes 90 and ci.yml:200-206 now deliberately fails on exit 4
:fix:          judge on a rate (syspolicyd CPU seconds per wall second of the window) or exclude the build from the window; recalibrate against measured 0.075 s/s ambient vs 0.35-0.96 s/s in-run
:END:

:SEVERITY:     MEDIUM
:KIND:         bug
:FILE:         crates/orgasmic-cli/src/manager.rs:5423
:END:

* TX 2026-08-06 Thu 21:17:49 reviewer.finding TASK-STWVB.1.1
:PROPERTIES:
:TX_ID:        tx-20260806-orgasmic-5066
:TIME:         [2026-08-06 Thu 21:17:49]
:TYPE:         reviewer.finding
:ACTOR:        theaspirational@users.noreply.github.com
:MACHINE:      Vasyls-MacBook-Pro.local
:PROJECT:      orgasmic
:TASK:         TASK-STWVB.1.1
:REASON:       M-2 BLOCK SHIP: host_judgment_measured ORs load|cpu|wall, so the summary word is 'calm' whenever the PRIMARY signal is unmeasured but load parsed. Probed: syspolicyd_cpu=? / wall_s missing / wall_s=0 / wall_s=-5 all print 'host : calm ... rate ?' and exit 0. This regresses STWVB.1/F3's fail-safe: any log stamped before this commit has no wall_s, so reclassifying it now reads 'calm' where it used to read 'unknown'. Same on Linux and on any host where pgrep -x syspolicyd misses (possibly the macos-15 runner), where ci.yml's deliberate exit-4 gate is silently inert while the line advertises a threshold. Fix: derive the word from the RATE - calm only when rate is numeric and below threshold, unknown otherwise.
:SEVERITY:     HIGH
:KIND:         correctness
:BLOCKS_SHIP:  yes
:LOC:          scripts/run-tests.sh:496-507,988
:END:

* TX 2026-08-06 Thu 21:17:50 reviewer.finding TASK-STWVB.1.1
:PROPERTIES:
:TX_ID:        tx-20260806-orgasmic-5067
:TIME:         [2026-08-06 Thu 21:17:50]
:TYPE:         reviewer.finding
:ACTOR:        theaspirational@users.noreply.github.com
:MACHINE:      Vasyls-MacBook-Pro.local
:PROJECT:      orgasmic
:TASK:         TASK-STWVB.1.1
:REASON:       M-3: the rate has no minimum window. wall comes from date +%s (integer, +/-1 s) clamped to a floor of 1, and host_is_degraded gates at any wall. Probed: wall_s=1 cpu=2.0 -> DEGRADED exit 4; wall_s=3 cpu=4.5 -> rate 1.5000 -> DEGRADED exit 4. Empirically I could NOT induce a misfire: ambient peak 1 s-window rate 0.17 s/s over 83 s, and peak 0.25 s/s (mean 0.12) while 300 freshly linked Mach-Os were first-exec'd as a deliberate Gatekeeper scan storm - an order of magnitude under 1.50. But the chain's own thrash figure is ~5.6 s/s, so the ceiling is >=3.7x the threshold and a 1-3 s window landing in such a burst reads DEGRADED on 1-3 samples. Fix: require wall_s >= a floor (10-30 s) to gate at all; below it report host unknown (window too short to judge), not calm and not DEGRADED.
:SEVERITY:     MEDIUM
:KIND:         correctness
:BLOCKS_SHIP:  no
:LOC:          scripts/run-tests.sh:465-493,636-638
:END:

:TASK:         TASK-STWVB.1.1.1
:REASON:       One root cause in two forms. R-1: FAIL_COUNT counts only LISTED per-test failures and a crashed binary contributes none, so the restored guard suppresses the crash arm whenever anything else classifies — the normal case on a board with seven registered flakes. Reviewer reproduced GREEN modulo 1 registered flake at exit 0 over verbatim cargo output containing SIGABRT and 'error: 2 targets failed'. Manager confirmed: BUILD_BROKE matches only compile errors, and the script has ZERO crash-signal detection. R-2: same verdict for the same log is a real invariant and --classify violates it in the dangerous direction; the fix is to stamp the suite exit exactly as host state is already stamped. Reviewer correctly classifies R-1 as PRE-EXISTING rather than a regression: at 4788e1f the arm sat below FAIL_COUNT and was equally unreachable. All four of this round's fixes are correct and correctly pinned — do not re-open them, and do NOT re-drop the guard.

:TASK:         TASK-RMA18
:REASON:       F1 BLOCK SHIP: git_would_remove_worktree omits git's categorical submodule refusal, so prune recursively deletes worktrees a non-forced git worktree remove refuses (measured, git 2.52.0)
:SEVERITY:     HIGH
:KIND:         correctness
:VERDICT:      block-ship
:FILE:         crates/orgasmic-cli/src/manager.rs:3915-3979
:EVIDENCE:     probe: clean worktree with initialized submodule -> git status --porcelain empty, no locked marker, git worktree remove EXIT=128 'working trees containing submodules cannot be moved or removed', --force EXIT=0
:IMPACT:       prune deletes what dispatch-close (manager.rs:5775, still shells git worktree remove) refuses; with submodule.<n>.ignore=all committed in .gitmodules, uncommitted submodule work is invisible to git status and unsalvageable by parent git add -A
:FIX:          refuse initialized submodules (git validate_no_submodules equivalent) and pass --ignore-submodules=none to the status call; regression with a submodule sentinel
:END:

:PROPERTIES:

:TYPE:         reviewer.finding
:ACTOR:        theaspirational@users.noreply.github.com
:MACHINE:      Vasyls-MacBook-Pro.local

:REASON:       P1 crates/orgasmic-core/src/session.rs:1162-1165 and crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/recovery_claim.rs:1094-1122,1370-1392: the authoritative path ignores scan.truncated even though the scanner contract says the skipped middle is unknown. RecoveryOrigin follows an uncapped PromptDraft and embeds the same claim draft; after enough later events a valid link can sit outside both windows, be treated as absent, and have its live claim quarantined. Use a full or streaming authoritative fallback and add a greater-than-192-KiB production-shaped regression.

:KIND:         correctness

:TYPE:         reviewer.finding
:ACTOR:        theaspirational@users.noreply.github.com
:MACHINE:      Vasyls-MacBook-Pro.local

:REASON:       P2 crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/api.rs:10045-10068 and crates/orgasmic-daemon/src/recovery_claim.rs:1362-1372: inventory builds the catalog origin index once to avoid O(failed_runs times session_bytes), but each committed claim now re-enumerates every JSONL in its project inside apply_recovery_claim_to_run.
